target.title: fix(agents): time out local streams without first event
target.body:
Related: #97871

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local OpenAI-compatible streaming providers could open an HTTP SSE response and then never send the first stream event.
When that happened during `agent --local`, OpenClaw could appear to hang because local providers intentionally skip the normal inter-event idle watchdog.
This PR is AI-assisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a separate first-event timeout for the exact boundary where HTTP streaming headers have arrived but the provider body has not produced a parsed event.
It keeps the existing local-model inter-event idle behavior unchanged, so slow local prompt evaluation and thinking are still allowed after the first event arrives.

- Added a shared `withFirstStreamEventTimeout` stream wrapper.
- Reused it in Responses and OpenAI-compatible completions stream parsing.
- Resolved a bounded first-event timeout in the embedded runner and passed it through stream options.
- Kept local/self-hosted providers on a longer default first-event timeout than cloud providers.

## User Impact

Users should get a clear transport error instead of an apparent indefinite wait when a local provider commits to SSE but sends no first event.
Successful local streams and slow local inter-token generation should continue to behave as before.

## Evidence

Focused tests and build passed locally.
A manual local provider smoke also opened `text/event-stream` and sent no body; the provider returned `stopReason: "error"` with `completions HTTP stream opened but did not deliver a first SSE event...` instead of hanging.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/stream-first-event-timeout.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/llm-idle-timeout.test.ts`
- `pnpm build`
- `git diff --check`

The full CLI mock with a short `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds` was also tried. That path hits the existing fetch timeout first, so it does not prove the new first-event diagnostic; the provider-level smoke directly proves the new stream boundary.
